modules.title: Lesson 1: Defining Art
modules.summary: What art is, why it matters, what it is for, and how it is classified.

notes.title: Introduction
notes.content:
This lesson tackles **how art is defined**, **why it matters**, **what it is for**, and some **preliminary assumptions** people normally hold about art.

Guiding questions:
- How can we read and understand a work of art?
- What can we learn from studying art?

The goal is to recognize your own understanding of art and build a wider, more comprehensive view of the nature and definition of art through **visual analysis**: identifying, discussing, and clarifying views and perceptions about art.

notes.title: Defining Art
notes.content:
Art is all around us. It is **universal**: it can be found in **all cultures**.

> **Basic assumption #1:** Art is universal.

- Art has been around for **thousands of years** and has evolved in many different ways.
- The reasons for creating it vary from **person to person**, **culture to culture**, and **time period to time period**.

Imagine a world without art: how would things around us look? Would beauty or anything visually appealing exist at all? This provocative question is why we need to define what art **is** and **is not**.

notes.title: Why Art Matters
notes.content:
Art is so diverse that there are as many ways to understand it as there are people. Scholars from different fields give their own definitions, but the point is that **people look at art based on how they experience it**.

> **Basic assumption #2:** Art involves experience.

Art has both **purpose** and **expression**. It has a unique role in **moving people**:
- a source of **inspiration**
- inciting new questions and provoking **curiosity**
- revolutionary ideas, and **socio-cultural and political advocacies**
- an essential ingredient to **empowering people**, especially the younger generation

**Example:** When activists show images of **extrajudicial killings (EJK)** in their campaigns, art is pulling at the heartstrings of society, its government and its forces to push for radical change.

So art can influence **culture, politics, and even the economy**.

Art also develops **critical thinking** and the ability to **interpret the world** around us. Art requires thought, a kind of **creative impulse**: it is not limited to absorbing information; it makes you think about current ideas and inspires you to make your own. For students, art encourages **self-expression and creativity** and unlocks the potential of the human mind.

> **Basic assumption #3:** Art is a human creation, using our thoughtful skill and artistry.

notes.title: What Is Art Made For? (Functions of Art)
notes.content:
An inquiry on **what art is for** is an inquiry on the **function of art**.

- Every piece of art is functional in some way: **all art exists for a reason**, and these reasons make up the functions of art.
- No art can be "assigned" a function **outside of its proper context**. Art forms exist within very specific contexts that must be considered when classifying them.
- Different art forms come with distinctive functions.

The functions of art normally fall into **three categories**:

### 1. Personal function
- Highly varied and **subjective**; depends on the **artist** who creates it.
- Art made for **self-expression, enjoyment, provoking thought, or therapeutic purposes**.

### 2. Social function
- Art used for **public display and celebration**.
- Used to affect **collective behavior**: addresses a **collective interest** rather than one's personal point of view or experience.

### 3. Physical function
- Realized through the **objects and environments** we create that fill a **utilitarian need**.

notes.title: How Is Art Classified?
notes.content:
Traditional and contemporary art include activities as diverse as architecture, sculpture, painting, music, theater, dance, printmaking, opera, photography, literature, filmmaking, furniture, and ceramics.

They are commonly classified into **four categories**:

| Category | What it is | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Visual Arts** | Works that are **primarily visual** in nature | drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, printmaking, **architecture** |
| **2. Performing / Combined Arts** | Combine a variety of media that can be **both seen and heard**, existing in **both space and time** | music, dance, film, theater, literature |
| **3. Digital Arts** | Work **made with** or **presented on** digital technology | images made entirely on a computer or electronic device, shared on social media platforms |
| **4. Applied Art** | Artistic design **applied to utilitarian objects** of everyday use | furniture design, interior design, fashion design, graphic design |

⚠️ Watch out: **architecture** is listed under **Visual Arts** in this lesson, not Applied Art.

questions.prompt: According to the lesson, the functions of art normally fall into which three categories?
questions.explanation: The three categories of the functions of art are personal, social, and physical.

questions.prompt: Which function of art addresses a collective interest rather than one's personal point of view or experience?
questions.explanation: The social function affects collective behavior and is used for public display and celebration.

questions.prompt: Art realized through objects and environments that fill a utilitarian need serves which function?
An artist who creates art for self-expression, enjoyment, or therapeutic purposes is fulfilling which function of art?
questions.explanation: The personal function is subjective and depends on the artist who creates the art.

questions.prompt: Drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, printmaking, and architecture are classified under:
questions.explanation: These works are primarily visual in nature.

questions.prompt: Which category covers art forms that can be both seen and heard and exist in both space and time?
questions.explanation: Examples are music, dance, film, theater, and literature.

questions.prompt: Furniture design, interior design, fashion design, and graphic design are examples of:
questions.explanation: Applied art applies artistic design to utilitarian objects of everyday use.

questions.prompt: An image made entirely on a computer and shared on social media is classified as:
questions.explanation: Digital art is work made with or presented on digital technology.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is classified under Performing/Combined Arts in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Sculpture and printmaking are visual arts; interior design is applied art.

questions.prompt: In the lesson's example, activists showing images of extrajudicial killings (EJK) in their campaigns shows art's power to:
choices: Move people and push for social and political change
questions.answer: Move people and push for social and political change
questions.explanation: Art can influence culture, politics, and even the economy.

questions.prompt: Art is universal: it can be found in all cultures.
questions.explanation: This is one of the basic assumptions of art in the lesson.

questions.prompt: According to the lesson, a work of art can be assigned a function even outside of its proper context.
questions.explanation: No art can be assigned a function outside of the proper context.

questions.prompt: Architecture is classified under Applied Art in this lesson.
questions.explanation: The lesson lists architecture under Visual Arts.

questions.prompt: Art is limited to absorbing information.
questions.explanation: Art makes you think about current ideas and inspires you to make your own.

questions.prompt: The reasons for creating art vary from person to person, culture to culture, and time period to time period.
All art exists for a reason, and these reasons make up the functions of art.
An inquiry on what art is for is an inquiry on the ______ of art.
The category of art in which artistic design is applied to utilitarian objects of everyday use.
Since art can be found in all cultures, art is said to be ______.
Art is a human ______, utilizing our thoughtful skill and artistry.
Since people look at art based on how they experience it, art is said to involve ______.
Give the three categories of the functions of art.
Give the four general categories into which art is classified.
Give the three basic assumptions about art mentioned in the lesson.

flashcards.back: Art is universal: it can be found in all cultures.
Art involves experience: people look at art based on how they experience it.
Art is a human creation, using our thoughtful skill and artistry.
What art is for. All art exists for a reason, but no art can be assigned a function outside its proper context.
Subjective; depends on the artist. Art for self-expression, enjoyment, provoking thought, or therapy.
Public display and celebration; affects collective behavior and addresses a collective interest.
Objects and environments we create that fill a utilitarian need.
Primarily visual works: drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, printmaking, architecture.
Can be both seen and heard; exists in both space and time: music, dance, film, theater, literature.
Work made with or presented on digital technology.
Artistic design applied to everyday utilitarian objects: furniture, interior, fashion, graphic design.
Art moves people and can influence culture, politics, and even the economy.
